injection_rule.semantics: Each entry is a defect-dictionary row. `pattern` is the DEFECT text (a substitution template, backreferences \1..\9 allowed); `replacement` is the CORRECT text (a Python re search pattern). The mutant applier injects the defect into a pristine copy of the module by: re.sub(entry['replacement'], entry['pattern'], module_text). The search side is therefore the CORRECT form and the write side the DEFECT form. Site count = len(re.findall(entry['replacement'], module_text)). Zero sites => mutant classified not-applicable (recorded in the report debt register; judged per the contract exit-code matrix). All occurrences are substituted in one pass.
injection_rule.applier_scope: Whole-file text (module bytes decoded utf-8), single re.sub pass, re patterns must be single-line safe (no cross-line matches required in v1).
injection_rule.direction_rationale: The correct reciprocal pairing is power index 2*k+1 with reciprocal argument 2*k, because rsT_recipQ k = 1/(k+1) (cwb_rs_weighted.v:339-342) and rcp (k : nat) : Q := recip1 (rpn k) (cwb_cp89_lnkit.v:194) both add the +1 internally; the incident defect was writing the reciprocal argument as 2*k+1, double-shifting the denominator to 2*k+2.

mutants.name: off-by-one reciprocal index (canonical star, first-class)
mutants.evidence: face-T incident of cwb_rs_weighted.v: the odd term of index 2*k+1 must take its denominator through reciprocal argument 2*k (prose discipline at cwb_rs_weighted.v:339-341 'takes its denominator 2 * j + 1 through rsT_recipQ (2 * j)'; correct sites at cwb_rs_weighted.v:375 and :381; gated kit correct form at cwb_cp89_lnkit.v:479-486, sites :482 and :486; wrappers rsT_recipQ k = 1/(k+1) at cwb_rs_weighted.v:342 and rcp at cwb_cp89_lnkit.v:194). The defect turns the denominator 2*k+1 into 2*k+2, one off, matching the incident class.
mutants.expected_effect: Every odd series term evaluates smaller than declared (denominator 2*k+2 instead of 2*k+1); bracket/tail certificates computed over the suspect series flip at small-depth and boundary sample points; positivity-only certificates do NOT flip and are thereby exposed as VACUOUS.

mutants.name: denominator shift (geometric tail denominator perturbed)
mutants.evidence: Tail bounds in the corpus end in the geometric divisor '/ (1 - qpow_nat t 2)' (cwb_rs_weighted.v:380-382 rsT_atanhQ_tail; cwb_cp89_lnkit.v:485-486 atanhQ_tail). Shrinking the divisor's value by a constant understates the certified tail remainder.
mutants.expected_effect: Tail-inclusive brackets go under; certificates that check the bracket at the boundary corner flip; certificates ignoring the tail do not and are exposed as VACUOUS.

mutants.name: constant last-place perturbation (numerator +1, denominator pinned)
mutants.evidence: Canonical midpoint constant (1 # 2)%Q in Q-literal form; the v1 perturbation rule is numerator+1 with the denominator pinned (one ulp at fixed denominator). Manifest authors copy this entry and narrow the search regex to their own constant with the same numerator+1 rule.
mutants.expected_effect: Any certificate consuming the constant at a sample point computes a shifted value; exact-equality and tight-tolerance checks flip.

mutants.name: comparator swap (Qle_bool to Qlt_bool)
mutants.evidence: Non-strict vs strict rational comparators in gate faces; the boundary corner sample point (equality at the edge) is the designated catcher. Swap direction is frozen as Qle_bool -> Qlt_bool; a module whose certificates use Qlt_bool natively takes the inverse copy of this entry (pattern Qle_bool, replacement Qlt_bool) declared in its own manifest.
mutants.expected_effect: Gates that accept equality flip exactly at the boundary corner; certificates without a boundary point do not flip and are exposed as VACUOUS (this is why the coverage rule mandates a boundary case).

mutants.name: depth shift (K to pred K at evaluation sites)
mutants.evidence: Certified tail after depth K is t^(2K+1)/(2K+1)/(1-t^2) (cwb_rs_weighted.v:378-382; cwb_cp89_lnkit.v:472-477,485-486). Evaluating the tail at pred K claims a deeper-certified bracket than computed. Numeral call sites in certificate check terms make the shift visible to vm_compute; symbolic-K sites in lemma statements may stillborn (recorded, judged per the contract matrix).
mutants.expected_effect: Closed check terms with a numeral depth compute the shallower tail; tight brackets flip. Statement-site stillbirths are honest debt, not kills.

mutants.name: series-term drop (one odd addend zeroed)
mutants.evidence: Odd partial sums are built by one addend per successor step (cwb_rs_weighted.v:370-376 rsT_atanhQ_sum; cwb_cp89_lnkit.v:479-483 atanhQ_sum). Zeroing the addend keeps the module compiling and underestimates every partial sum at K >= 1.
mutants.expected_effect: All lower-bracket checks at K >= 1 flip; upper-only or positivity certificates do not and are exposed as VACUOUS.

mutants.name: lemma-form parity mismatch (odd-power shape to even)
mutants.evidence: R2-131 expansion. Parity-shape face of the suspect series power term: canonical correct form qpow_nat t (2 * k + 1) (recorded verbatim inside the frozen DROP-001/DEN-001 evidence citing cwb_rs_weighted.v:370-382 and cwb_cp89_lnkit.v:472-486). The defect states the lemma/certificate shape with the even power 2*k where the certified bound is the odd power 2*k+1. Distinct from OB1-001 (reciprocal argument), DEN-001 (geometric divisor), DEP-001 (call-site depth), DROP-001 (addend drop). Direction frozen (2*k+1) -> (2*k); a module needing the inverse direction declares the mirror copy in its own manifest.
mutants.expected_effect: For 0 < t < 1 the even power exceeds the odd power, so tail-inclusive upper bounds overstate; upper-bound and tight-boundary certificates flip at depth >= 1 sample points; lower-bracket-only and positivity-only certificates do not flip and are exposed as VACUOUS.

mutants.name: projection swap (proj1 to proj2, frozen direction; author-narrowed site)
mutants.evidence: R2-131 expansion, CONST-001 author-narrowing precedent: manifest authors copy this entry and narrow the search regex to their module's compute-face consumption sites (for example 'proj1 \\(bracket_pair half\\)'), keeping class semantic; the defect is the whole-match span replay 'proj2 (bracket_pair half)' so the argument is not swallowed (re.sub replaces the entire match). The blanket form is proven fragile by the R2-131 live probe: on a module whose record declares a proj1 field the generic swap breaks the declaration (duplicate field name, compile rc 1, stillborn, debt register). Proof-position (tactic-level) proj swaps remain out of v1 scope per the frozen excluded_classes note. Direction frozen proj1 -> proj2; a module whose certificates consume proj2 natively declares the inverse copy in its own manifest.
mutants.expected_effect: Swapping the projection at a compute-face site exchanges the pair components the certificate consumes, so sample-point checks consuming the first component flip wherever the two components differ; certificates consuming both components symmetrically or neither do not flip and are exposed as VACUOUS.

excluded_classes.reason: Proof-tactic defects change how a statement is proven, not what the certificate computes; they are out of v1 scope and recorded as future work. Only class "semantic" is accepted in manifests; any other class value is a usage error (exit 2).

independence_note: Anchors must derive their certificate independently of the suspect series (atanh vs Mercator is the named exemplar). This library carries no mechanical independence check in v1; the requirement is an authoring obligation verified by review and recorded verbatim in the report.
